# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 63 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 63 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_063_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 1 — Keep Your Body Pure

**63:1** I was sitting at home, praising God for everything I had seen and turning the commandments over in my mind — how beautiful, powerful, joyful, and glorious they were, how capable of saving a person's soul. I thought to myself: anyone who lives by these commandments will be truly blessed. Blessed will be all who walk in them.

**63:2** While I was thinking this, I saw him sitting next to me. He said: "Why are you still doubting the commandments I gave you? They're beautiful. Stop wavering — clothe yourself in the Lord's faith and walk in them. I will make you strong in them."

**63:3** "Lord," I said, "this commandment especially resonates with me, because I've never sinned against it in my entire life." "Say more," he said. "I have always kept myself sexually pure," I said, "right up to this day — free from women, from adultery, from every form of sexual impurity." He was pleased and said: "Good — you say this because you haven't sinned. But let me add something else: you must also keep your body itself pure and undefiled, so that the Spirit living in it can bear testimony to it and your body may be justified."

**63:4** "Be careful," he said. "Don't let any thought get into your mind that treats your body as already defiled. Because if a pure body is contaminated by an evil thought, it brings death. Keep it pure, and believe: if you keep your body pure, you will live for God."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing Hermas's practical purity instruction at the transition to Similitude 6.*
